note: The journalist's desk: the cycle every evidence export goes through, the full pass and where it stands, and the pass ledger, one row per hand-kept data file with the evidence vault head it was last checked against. Kept by claude-journalist. The staleness report on /views/desk/ is computed from this file, the built pages and the vault's claims at every build.
author: claude-journalist

decided.says: the journalist does the full pass and maintains the site after each export as part of its workflow, released in turn rather than in one large push

cycle.label: Watch
cycle.what: The source watch re-reads every outside page on a schedule and keeps a dated snapshot when one changes.

cycle.label: Curate
cycle.what: Five times a day the curator promotes about 18 snapshots into the evidence vault, reads each, and records its claims and timeline rows.

cycle.label: Export
cycle.what: The journalist pulls the evidence vault read-only and re-exports it into data/: sources, counts, claims, timeline, the latest capture.

cycle.label: Review
cycle.what: Every new vault claim appears on /claims/review/ as not yet reviewed; each gets a verdict (used, agrees, held back) checked against the saved page and the ledger.

cycle.label: Refresh
cycle.what: The hand-kept data files the new evidence touches are updated, each row citing a capture, and the pass ledger below records the head each was checked against.

cycle.label: State
cycle.what: When the evidence moves enough to change what a reader should know, a new version of the state of affairs is written; its delta is on /views/.

cycle.label: Release
cycle.what: Build, gate, security check, release.sh to dev, check live. One step of the pass per release, not one large push.

cycle.label: Settled
cycle.what: The staleness report on this page is empty: no 'as of' older than the latest capture, every file checked against the current head, every vault claim reviewed.

pass.title: The desk, the plan and the staleness report
pass.what: This page: the cycle, the pass, the pass ledger and the report that says what is still stale.

pass.title: Refresh the hand-kept data from the new evidence
pass.what: Story, the compromise line, the offline ledger, agencies, numbers, the timeline, the KEV snapshot and the software inventory, each checked against the current head.

pass.title: Move the facts typed into the build into data
pass.what: Front-page tiles, KEV, playbook, the Explained page, chart windows and counts read from data, so the next export changes them without code.

pass.title: The persona pass
pass.what: The sixteen readers' answers, introductions and asks move into personas.json, with their 'as of' generated, and are re-read against the state of affairs.

pass.title: Review the rest of the curator's claims
pass.what: Every claim on /claims/review/ gets a verdict; the used ones go into the site's claim table with their sources.

kept_as_written_why: Stories, updates, versions of the state of affairs, release notes, briefs, outside readings and source pages are dated and kept as written by design; a dated phrase in them is history, not staleness. Facts pages carry every version of a fact. The state of affairs gives each measure its own as-of time on purpose.

accepted.why: Huntress's own time for its statement that it had seen no exploitation on its partners' systems (claim huntress-none): a source's date, kept wherever the claim is quoted.
